text: What is CPI? Consumer price index report due Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026. CPI is the Consumer Price Index, a monthly measure of how much prices paid by American households have risen or fallen. The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the October 2026 CPI report on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time.. The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the October consumer price index on Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting on Dec. 8 and 9. Markets are pricing a better than 80 percent chance of a rate increase in December.. The index tracks the cost of a broad basket of goods and services, from gasoline and groceries to rent and medical care. Economists compare each month's reading with the month before, and the report is the main public gauge of inflation that the Federal Reserve follows closely. A separate "core" figure, which leaves out food and energy, is forecast to rise 0.2 percent, against 0.3 percent in September. Gasoline fell more than 4 percent in October according to the Energy Information Administration, and AAA put the average regular gasoline price at $4.32 a gallon, though gasoline still cost 40 percent more than a year earlier. No year-over-year comparison will be published for October. The government shutdown that ran from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025 kept the Bureau of Labor Statistics from collecting some data, so an annual rate cannot be compared directly. The report matters now because it is the last CPI release before the Fed meets on Dec. 8 and 9. Policymakers have broadly signaled a rate increase next month, and Fed governor Christopher J. Waller said a half-point increase is possible if core prices rise 0.3 percent or more. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said the price pressures had spread into services and linked them to AI data center construction.
